event_note: The operator asked for the event to be treated as real, so it is. The date and session are NOT confirmed, and the evidence points to after the close, not before the open. Last year's Q2 release went out 2025-10-13 at 4:05 PM (finviz) with the call the next morning. The Q1 FY27 print on 2026-07-14 is tagged amc in the baseline. MarketBeat estimates Tue 2026-10-13 bmo 'based on past reporting schedules'. As of 2026-10-09 no scheduling release is on ir.rmcf.com, although the Q1 release said a Q2 call is expected and prior years announced the call about 7-11 days ahead. The 10-Q is due 2026-10-15 (Aug 31 + 45 days), so a print in the week of 10-12 is near-certain. If it comes 10-12 after the close or later, the 10-09 close to 10-12 close window carries no print.
conviction_note: No consensus exists and no company-level number is unpriced. What remains are small inferences that roughly offset: royalty attrition from the revised franchise agreements and transition and strategic-review costs on the negative side, against an easy product-margin comp, the debt clean-up and strategic-review optionality on the positive side. impact_sum -0.5 and the scaled number -0.52 (p_up 46 x abs 6.5) agree. abs_move is set above the 4.37% median for thin turnover (~$100k/day) and the first call under the interim CEO. p_up sits only slightly below 50 because the bar is unsourced and the +20% five-day run-up on the sale-leaseback cuts both ways.
bar: unsourced: no analyst consensus exists (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RMCF/earnings/ shows dashes for every quarter; Yahoo and Benzinga show none). The only reference is the year-ago Q2 FY26: revenue $6.823m, EPS -$0.09 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001616262/000143774925030944/ex_869724.htm). print_vs_bar_pct is against that year-ago revenue, and every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 63.9K shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement, 1.9 days to cover; 38.0K at 08-31; a one-off 570.5K at 08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/rmcf/short-interest/, read 2026-10-09). That is about 0.7% of 9.44m shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 2026-07-07): not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. No options market, so no skew. The tape shows +20.45% over 5d and +17.78% over 20d into the print, at $1.06, -63.6% off the 52-week high. The five-day move follows the 2026-10-06 sale-leaseback 8-K. Concentrated insider and activist holders: interim CEO Harper's family (~13%), Geygan/GVIC, Craig.

findings.finding: Royalty and marketing fees are falling structurally under revised franchise agreements: Q1 FY27 franchise and royalty fees were $1.232m vs $1.655m (-26%). Units also fell 253 -> 250 in Q1, including Cold Stone co-branded 101 -> 98. Against Q2 FY26's $1.640m royalty line that is roughly -$0.4m of revenue. Net of product sales up ~3% on price, Q2 revenue likely prints below last year's $6.82m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (revenue -4% YoY, wider loss) drew -1.96% (baseline, 2026-07-14). The Q3 FY26 print drew -7.01% (2026-01-13).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Q1 decline is public. The second quarter of royalty attrition, against the highest royalty comp of the year ($1.64m), has not been written anywhere because no one models the name. If it were priced, the stock would not have run +20% in five days into a print whose top line is likely down YoY.
findings.independence: The unit counts come from the same company document, the Q1 FY27 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000119312526303159/rmcf-20260531.htm). Same company, different filing: not independent evidence. Net of the rest: product and retail sales (~80% of revenue) rose 3% in Q1, so the net revenue effect is about -4%, not -6%.

findings.finding: Q2 FY26 product and retail gross profit was negative (-$33k on $5.18m of sales), an easy comp. ICE cocoa traded around $5,000/t in mid-2026, against a 52-week high of $8,823, so a lagged input-cost tailwind is plausible. Against this, Q1 FY27 product margin fell to ~3.7% from ~6.9% despite cheaper cocoa.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin narrative on the FY26 print ('strongest product margin profile in two years') drew -5.08% (2026-06-01, baseline). Margin has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes a margin estimate for this name, and the company has not mentioned cocoa in its last two releases. Partly priced in the sense that the commodity decline is public.
findings.independence: Cocoa price is a proxy: https://fr.investing.com/commodities/us-cocoa (CCU6 ~5,156, 52-week range 2,846-8,823; undated snapshot). The company's own Q1 FY27 margin moved the other way, so the transmission is unconfirmed and sized small.

findings.finding: The $6.6m Durango sale-leaseback (closing ~2026-10-15) repays the 12% notes held by entities affiliated with directors Craig and Geygan. Those notes carry the breached liabilities-to-tangible-net-worth covenant (5.3:1 vs 2.0:1, waived only through 2026-08-31). The Q2 10-Q must therefore address covenant status and going concern with this as a subsequent event. Interest of ~$792k a year is replaced by $624k of rent rising 2% a year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing. The announcement itself coincides with the +20% five-day run-up in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the deal was on the wire on 10-06 and the stock rose ~20% in five sessions. What is not yet visible is how the 10-Q words the covenant waiver and going concern. Asked what the money buys: it removes a breached, related-party 12% debt and the covenant overhang. It does not fund growth. The company gives up its main hard asset and takes on a change-of-control buy-back at the greater of $6.93m or appraised value. Net sign: slightly positive, mostly in the price.
findings.independence: Covenant facts come from the Q1 FY27 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000119312526303159/rmcf-20260531.htm). Press release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000121390026107214/ea030780001ex99-1.htm (same deal).

findings.finding: The board is running a strategic-alternatives review that includes a possible sale, with expressions of interest received (8-K 2026-08-12). The new lease's change-of-control buy-back clause shows a transaction is being planned for. Any update alongside the print, or on the first Q2 call under interim CEO Harper, is upside optionality.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the review has been public since August and the stock sits about 58% above its 52-week low. The company also said it will not update unless a transaction is approved, so the expected value inside the window is small and the tail is wide.
findings.independence: Change-of-control clause in the sale-leaseback 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000121390026107214/ea0307800-8k_rocky.htm). A different filing, but the same issuer.

findings.finding: Q2 costs carry several leadership and process changes: interim CEO Harper from 2026-06-30 (a 180-day term), a new COO on 2026-08-24, an auditor change on 2026-06-12, strategic-review advisers, and litigation professional fees cited in the FY26 release. Q1 FY27's operating loss had already widened to -$1.006m from -$0.145m. The Q2 loss is likely worse than last year's -$0.09/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wider losses: Q1 FY27 -1.96%, Q3 FY26 -7.01%.
findings.why_not_priced: No one estimates the loss. The run-up after the sale-leaseback suggests holders are trading the balance-sheet fix and the sale process, not the P&L. A priced loss would show up as a tape that had not rallied into the print.
findings.independence: COO appointment: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000121390026092815/ea030293701ex99-1.htm (2026-08-24). Litigation fees: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000143774926018927/ex_970190.htm (2026-06-01). The cost size is inference.

outside_window.finding: Sale-leaseback closing 'on or about 2026-10-15': cash moves and notes repaid. Whether the related-party put-like buy-back clause allows sale accounting and a gain that rebuilds equity is a Q3 matter.

Nasdaq equity cushion: stockholders' equity was $4.144m at 2026-05-31 and falls about $1m a quarter. A Q2 loss leaves it near $3m, still above the $2.5m Capital Market minimum. A breach is a Q3 (Nov 30) risk, visible in January 2027.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 1: it lands on the same royalty line.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative against a +20% five-day run-up, with no skew to read. The run-up is a known event (the sale-leaseback), not a priced disappointment. That argues for a modest give-back but is not evidence, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced, no consensus anywhere): capped the two reported-quarter negatives, royalty attrition -0.8 -> -0.6 and costs/one-offs -0.6 -> -0.5, and moved p_up 45 -> 46
Rule 5 (proxy vs company number): cocoa tailwind +0.4 -> +0.2, because the company's own Q1 product margin fell despite cheaper cocoa
Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered. The money retires breached, related-party 12% debt and does not fund growth, and it is already in the run-up. Sign kept slightly positive, +0.3 -> +0.2
Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number): strategic review +0.3 -> +0.2, since the company said it will not update unless a deal is approved
Rule 9 (net of the rest): royalty finding sized net of product sales up ~3%
Rule 8 and the core: abs_move kept at 6.5, above the 4.37% median, for thin turnover; not shrunk for sign uncertainty
